## Background

The tutors-sdk (https://github.com/tutors-sdk) converts a folder of learning content into a web-based course. The folder structure uses naming conventions to identify content types. A non-technical user wouldn't know these conventions, so this wizard walks them through it.

## Course Folder Structure (what we generate)

```
my-course/
  course.md          # "# Title\nDescription"
  course.png         # Placeholder image
  properties.yaml    # credits, auth level, etc.
  
  topic-01-name/
    topic.md         # "# Topic Title\nSummary"
    topic.png        # Placeholder image
    unit-1/
      unit.md        # "Unit Title"
      talk-1-name/
        talk.md      # "Talk Title\nSummary"
        talk.pdf     # Placeholder PDF
        talk.png     # Placeholder image
      book-a/        # This is a "lab"
        00.Lab.md    # "# Lab Title\nObjectives"
        01.Step-01.md # "# Step 1\nContent"
        02.Step-02.md # "# Step 2\nContent"
        img/
          main.png   # Lab card image
    unit-2/
      ...
  topic-02-name/
    ...
```

Key content types and their folder prefixes:
- `topic-*` — major course section (contains units)
- `unit-*` — grouping within a topic (contains talks, labs, notes)
- `talk-*` — lecture/presentation (needs .md, .pdf, .png)
- `book-*` or `lab-*` — multi-step lab walkthrough (needs numbered .md files + img/main.png)
- `note-*` — rich markdown note (needs .md, .png)
- `web-*` — external link (needs .md, .png, weburl file)
- `github-*` — GitHub repo link (needs .md, .png, githubid file)
- `panelnote`, `paneltalk`, `panelvideo` — panel-level items in topics

1. **Ink-based React terminal UI** with a multi-step wizard flow
2. **Package name**: `create-tutors-course` (for `npx create-tutors-course`)
3. **TypeScript** with tsx or ts-node for execution
4. **Wizard steps**:

   - Step 2: Topic planning (how many topics, name each one)
   - Step 3: For each topic, configure content (how many talks, labs, notes per unit)
   - Step 4: Review summary and confirm
   - Step 5: Generate the folder structure with placeholder content
5. **Generated content should be valid** — the tutors CLI (`deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors`) should be able to process it
6. **Placeholder images** — generate simple colored PNG placeholders (use a library or embed minimal PNGs)
7. **Cross-platform** — works on macOS, Windows, Fedora

## Tech Stack Decisions
- Ink v5 for terminal UI (React-based)
- TypeScript compiled with tsup or tsc
- YAML generation with js-yaml
- Placeholder image generation (consider sharp, or embed a tiny 1x1 PNG and scale)

1. **Project structure** — folder layout, package.json shape, tsconfig, build config
2. **Wizard flow** — detailed step-by-step screens with what each collects
3. **State management** — how wizard state is tracked across steps
4. **Folder generation** — the module that takes wizard answers and creates the file tree
5. **Key components** — Ink React components needed (TextInput, SelectInput, MultiStep wrapper, etc.)
6. **Build and distribution** — how to build and publish for npx usage

## Context

The tutors-sdk converts a folder of learning content into a web-based course, but the folder structure uses specific naming conventions (`topic-*`, `unit-*`, `talk-*`, `book-*`, etc.) that a non-technical user wouldn't know. This CLI wizard walks someone through creating a valid course skeleton by asking questions about their course — title, topics, labs, talks — and generates the correctly-structured folder tree with placeholder content ready for the tutors generator.

## Tech Stack

- **Ink 5.x** + **React 18** — rich terminal UI with interactive forms
- **@inkjs/ui 2.x** — production-ready TextInput, Select, ConfirmInput, Spinner components
- **pngjs** — pure-JS PNG generation (no native deps, cross-platform)
- **js-yaml** — YAML generation for `properties.yaml`
- **tsup** — bundles everything into a single `dist/cli.js` for fast `npx` startup
- **Distribution**: `npx create-tutors-course` (npm's `create-*` convention)

## Project Structure

```
create-tutors-course/
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
  tsup.config.ts
  src/
    cli.tsx                    # Entry point (shebang injected by tsup)
    app.tsx                    # Root component: useReducer + step routing
    state/
      wizard-state.ts          # Types, reducer, React context
    steps/
      step-course-details.tsx  # Step 1: title, description, credits
      step-topic-planning.tsx  # Step 2: number of topics, name each
      step-topic-content.tsx   # Step 3: per-topic units/talks/labs/notes
      step-review.tsx          # Step 4: summary tree + confirm
      step-generate.tsx        # Step 5: progress spinner, file creation
    components/
      wizard-chrome.tsx        # Header, step indicator, footer wrapper
      labeled-input.tsx        # Label + TextInput
      number-input.tsx         # Numeric input with min/max/default
      step-indicator.tsx       # Visual "Step 2 of 5" progress bar
    generator/
      generate-course.ts       # async generator yielding progress events
      templates.ts             # .md / .yaml content templates
      placeholder-image.ts     # pngjs solid-color PNG (300x170)
    utils/
      slugify.ts               # text → folder-safe slug
```

## Wizard Flow (5 Steps)

**Step 1 — Course Details**: Title (required), description (required), credits/author (optional). Sequential field focus — Enter advances to next field.

**Step 2 — Topic Planning**: "How many topics?" (number input, 1–20, default 3), then name each topic with a TextInput. Completed topics show with green checkmarks.

**Step 3 — Topic Content**: For each topic: how many units → for each unit: title, number of talks (name each), number of labs (name each + step count), number of notes (name each). Defaults are aggressive (1 unit, 1 talk, 0 labs, 0 notes) so pressing Enter repeatedly produces a reasonable skeleton.

**Step 4 — Review**: Tree view of the entire course structure with total counts. ConfirmInput to proceed or go back.

**Step 5 — Generate**: Spinner with file-by-file progress. Creates the full folder tree, then shows path and next-steps instructions (`deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors` or Vercel deploy).

## Generated Folder Structure (example)

```
web-development-101/
  course.md               # "# Web Development 101\nLearn web dev..."
  course.png              # 300x170 cornflower blue placeholder
  properties.yaml         # credits, auth level
  topic-01-introduction/
    topic.md              # "# Introduction\nTopic summary"
    topic.png
    unit-1/
      unit.md             # "Main Lesson"
      talk-1-welcome/
        welcome.md        # "# Welcome\nA short summary."
        welcome.pdf       # Minimal valid PDF placeholder
        welcome.png
      book-a/
        00.Setup-Lab.md   # "# Objectives\n..."
        01.Step-01.md     # "# Step 1\n..."
        02.Step-02.md
        img/
          main.png        # Plum-colored placeholder
  topic-02-html-basics/
    ...
```

## Key Implementation Details

- **State**: Single `useReducer` in `<App>`, shared via React context. State type tracks `courseTitle`, `topics[]` (each with `units[]`, each with `items[]`).
- **Generator**: `async function* generateCourse(state, outputDir)` yields `{type, path, current, total}` events — the Step 5 component consumes these to update the spinner.
- **Placeholder images**: `pngjs` generates solid-color PNGs (different color per content type). No native dependencies.
- **Placeholder PDFs**: Embedded ~200-byte valid PDF buffer constant — just enough for the tutors generator to accept.
- **Build**: `tsup` bundles all deps into one file with `noExternal: [/.*/]` for fast npx cold-start. Shebang injected via `banner`.
- **Cross-platform**: `path.join()` everywhere, `\n` line endings, `fs.mkdirSync({recursive: true})`, pure-JS dependencies only.

## Implementation Order

1. Scaffold: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `tsup.config.ts`, `npm install`
2. Core types and state: `wizard-state.ts`
3. Entry points: `cli.tsx`, `app.tsx`
4. Shared components: `wizard-chrome.tsx`, `labeled-input.tsx`, `number-input.tsx`, `step-indicator.tsx`
5. Generator + templates: `generate-course.ts`, `templates.ts`, `placeholder-image.ts`, `slugify.ts`
6. Steps 1–5 in order, testing each incrementally
7. Build and test: `npm run build` → `node dist/cli.js` → verify generated folder with tutors CLI

## Verification

1. `npm run build` succeeds with no errors
2. `node dist/cli.js` launches the wizard, all 5 steps work
3. Generated folder structure matches tutors-sdk conventions (correct folder prefixes, required files present)
4. `deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors` processes the generated course without errors (if deno available, otherwise structural validation)
5. Test on Windows (current machine) — Mac/Linux are covered by pure-JS deps and `path.join()`

An interactive CLI wizard that helps you scaffold a [tutors-sdk](https://github.com/tutors-sdk) course folder structure — no knowledge of the tutors file conventions required.

The wizard walks you through naming your course, defining topics, and configuring content (talks, labs, notes) for each topic. It then generates the complete folder tree with placeholder markdown, images, and PDFs, ready for you to fill in your content and run the tutors generator.

## Quick Start

```bash
npx create-tutors-course
```

Or install globally:

```bash
npm install -g create-tutors-course
create-tutors-course
```

### Custom output directory

```bash
npx create-tutors-course --output-dir /path/to/output
```

## Wizard Flow

The wizard guides you through 5 steps:

| Step | What it asks |
|------|-------------|
| **1. Course Details** | Title, description, and author/credits |
| **2. Topics** | How many topics and a title for each |
| **3. Content** | For each topic: units, talks, labs (with step count), and notes |
| **4. Review** | Summary tree of the entire course — confirm or go back |
| **5. Generate** | Creates the folder structure with progress feedback |

## What Gets Generated

The wizard produces a folder structure that the [tutors generator](https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors-apps) can process directly:

```
my-course/
  course.md                              # Course title and description
  course.png                             # Placeholder card image
  properties.yaml                        # Course configuration

  topic-01-introduction/
    topic.md
    topic.png
    unit-1/
      unit.md
      talk-1-welcome/
        welcome.md                       # Talk title and summary
        welcome.pdf                      # Placeholder slides
        welcome.png
      book-a/                            # Lab
        00.setup-lab.md                  # Objectives
        01.Step-01.md                    # Lab steps
        02.Step-02.md
        img/
          main.png                       # Lab card image

  topic-02-html-basics/
    ...
```

## After Generating

1. **Edit the markdown files** to add your actual content
2. **Replace placeholder images** (`.png` files) with your own
3. **Replace placeholder PDFs** with your lecture slides
4. **Generate the course:**

```bash
cd my-course
npx -y deno-bin@latest run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors
```

This produces a `json/` folder that the [Tutors Reader](https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors) can serve, or deploy via Vercel/GitHub Pages.

## Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lgriffin/tutors-assistant.git
cd tutors-assistant
npm install
npm run build
node dist/cli.js
```

Watch mode for development:

```bash
npm run dev
# In another terminal:
node dist/cli.js
```

## Tech Stack

- [Ink 5](https://github.com/vadimdemedes/ink) — React for interactive terminal UIs
- [@inkjs/ui](https://github.com/vadimdemedes/ink-ui) — TextInput, Spinner, ConfirmInput components
- [pngjs](https://github.com/lukeapage/pngjs) — Pure-JS PNG generation (no native deps)
- [js-yaml](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml) — YAML generation for `properties.yaml`
- [tsup](https://github.com/egoist/tsup) — TypeScript bundler

## Platform Support

Works on macOS, Windows, and Linux. All dependencies are pure JavaScript — no native compilation required.
